newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 14.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5649. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- Hwang Jang-yop, a North Korean official seeking asylum at the South Korean embassy in Beijing, wrote in a letter he decided to defect in May last year when North Korean authorities began to attack his views as incompatible with the ruling establishment. The missive was written in October and received by The Chosun Ilbo through a middle man, the daily reported.
- The Seoul government on Thursday sent Kim Ha-jung, special advisor to South Korean Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha, to Bejing to facilitate Hwang Jang-yop's safe passage to Seoul.

- State prosecutors on Thursday arrested former Home Affairs minister Kim Woo-suk and two leading lawmakers from both opposition and ruling parties on charges of accepting bribes from Hanbo Group founder, Chung Tae-soo.

- The Ministry of Finance and Economy announced on Thursday stock trading regulations that will lower capital requirements for setting up new security firms. This will go into effect from the start of April.
